title: The Glass Drop That Shrugs Off a Hammer but Shatters at Its Tail
summary: A translation of the same day's science episode. When molten glass drips into cold water, it hardens into a tadpole-shaped drop. You can hit its head with a hammer and it won't break, yet snapping the thin tail turns the whole drop to powder in a fraction of a second. The episode follows the puzzle from the seventeenth-century Royal Society and Hooke's Micrographia to the photoelastic measurements of twenty sixteen. It explains how the fast-cooled outer skin locks into compression around an interior under tension, why a crack can only win once it reaches that tensile core, and how the same principle lives on in tempered glass.
